title: Career Roadmap · Electrolyser Design Engineer
summary: An Electrolyser Design Engineer designs, develops, tests and improves equipment that uses electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. When powered by renewable electricity, this process can produce green hydrogen, which may be used in industrial processes, energy storage, refining, fertilizer production and certain transport applications.

facts.Current degree: B.Tech / B.E. in Hydrogen & Fuel Cell Technology

about.label: Industry
about.text: Green hydrogen, renewable energy, electrochemical engineering, industrial gas production

about.label: Core Focus
about.text: Electrolyser systems, electrochemical cells, materials, thermal and fluid systems, process design

about.label: Career Outlook
about.text: An emerging engineering specialization linked to low-carbon hydrogen production and industrial decarbonization

blocks.text: An Electrolyser Design Engineer designs, develops, tests and improves equipment that uses electricity to split water into hydrogen and oxygen. When powered by renewable electricity, this process can produce green hydrogen, which may be used in industrial processes, energy storage, refining, fertilizer production and certain transport applications.
The role combines electrochemistry, mechanical and chemical engineering, materials science, electrical systems, fluid management and process safety.

blocks.label: Recommended starting focus
blocks.text: Electrochemical fundamentals, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, materials, CAD, process modelling and hydrogen safety.

rows.text: Continued development and demonstration of alkaline and PEM electrolysers, manufacturing scale-up and efficiency improvements
Potential expansion of large-scale hydrogen projects, renewable-power integration and electrolyser supply chains
Further development of durable catalysts, advanced membranes, system integration and lower-cost hydrogen production
Potential advances in high-efficiency electrolysis, industrial heat integration and next-generation electrochemical systems

blocks.text: These are indicative technology and industry scenarios, not guaranteed market growth or employment outcomes.
Year 1 — Engineering and Scientific Foundations

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Build a foundation in chemistry, physics, mathematics and engineering.

rows.text: Calculus, differential equations, linear algebra and numerical methods
Electrochemistry, chemical bonding, oxidation-reduction reactions and pH
Engineering mechanics, material science and technical drawing
Python, numerical calculations and data visualization
Excel, MATLAB or Python-based scientific computing

blocks.text: Projects

items.text: Calculate the theoretical energy requirements for splitting water.
Build a spreadsheet to estimate hydrogen production from electrical energy input.
Study how temperature and current affect basic electrochemical cell performance.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Understand the scientific principles of water electrolysis and energy conversion.
Year 2 — Electrochemistry and Electrolyser Components

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Understand how electrolyser cells work and how their components are selected.

rows.text: Electrode reactions, overpotential, Faraday's laws and current density
Alkaline, proton exchange membrane (PEM), anion exchange membrane (AEM) and solid oxide electrolysis
Catalysts, electrodes, membranes, separators and corrosion-resistant materials
Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, entropy and heat balance
Water flow, gas flow, pressure drop and mass transfer
CAD modelling, tolerances, drawings and component selection

blocks.text: Projects

items.text: Create a comparative study of alkaline and PEM electrolysers.
Calculate theoretical hydrogen output using Faraday's law.
Design a conceptual cell assembly in CAD.
Analyze the effects of current density and temperature on cell voltage using published experimental data.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Explain the components of an electrolyser and the major trade-offs involved in their design.
Year 3 — System Design, Modelling and Performance Optimization

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Move from individual cells to complete electrolyser systems.

rows.text: Cell geometry, stack compression, flow distribution and electrical connections
Voltage losses, current density, efficiency and hydrogen production rates
Heat generation, cooling requirements and temperature control
Water quality, circulation, purification and gas-liquid separation
Pressure, temperature, flow, voltage and current sensors
Piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), process flow diagrams and mass balances
MATLAB/Simulink, suitable process simulators and CAD tools

blocks.text: Major projects

items.text: Develop a mathematical model of a PEM or alkaline electrolyser.
Design a preliminary stack layout and estimate its operating parameters.
Model hydrogen production under variable renewable electricity input.
Create a simplified process flow diagram for an electrolyser plant, including water treatment, gas separation and cooling.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Build a documented model that connects operating conditions to hydrogen output, energy consumption and thermal behaviour.
Year 4 — Advanced Design and Industry Readiness
For a three-year or shorter degree structure, adapt these activities to the final year or final two semesters.

blocks.label: Primary objective
blocks.text: Develop a specialization and complete a realistic electrolyser engineering project.

rows.text: Improve efficiency, durability, cost or component performance
Study catalyst loading, membrane durability and degradation
Connect electrolyser models to renewable power and power electronics
Learn hydrogen leak prevention, ventilation, pressure protection and hazard analysis
Develop test plans, analyze performance data and document results
Complete a cell, stack, component or system-level design project
Pursue internships, research projects and technical interviews

blocks.label: Recommended capstone
blocks.text: Design and Performance Modelling of a Renewable-Powered PEM Electrolyser.
Include a system diagram, operating assumptions, model validation against published data, hydrogen output estimates, energy consumption, heat balance and a preliminary safety review.
1. Electrolyser Stack Design Engineer
Develops the cell stack, electrode assemblies, separators, membranes and supporting mechanical structures.

blocks.label: Core skills
blocks.text: Electrochemistry, materials, CAD, current distribution and stack assembly.
2. Electrochemical Materials Engineer
Works on catalysts, membranes, electrodes, coatings and degradation-resistant materials.

blocks.label: Core skills
blocks.text: Materials science, electrochemical testing, corrosion and material characterization.
3. Process and Systems Design Engineer
Designs the supporting systems for water treatment, cooling, gas separation, purification and hydrogen delivery.

blocks.label: Core skills
blocks.text: Mass and energy balances, fluid mechanics, process simulation and P&IDs.
4. Electrolyser Controls and Integration Engineer
Integrates power electronics, sensors and control systems to manage operating conditions and changing electricity supply.

blocks.label: Core skills
blocks.text: Control systems, instrumentation, electrical engineering, data acquisition and simulation.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Electrolyser systems and performance modelling. This gives students a broad understanding of stack operation, energy efficiency and balance-of-plant requirements before they specialize.

blocks.label: PEM electrolysis
blocks.text: Compact systems with dynamic operating capabilities and precious-metal catalyst considerations.

blocks.label: Alkaline electrolysis
blocks.text: Established technology with ongoing opportunities to improve efficiency, cost and manufacturing.

blocks.label: Anion exchange membrane electrolysis
blocks.text: An evolving approach that aims to combine useful features of alkaline and membrane-based systems.

blocks.label: Solid oxide electrolysis
blocks.text: High-temperature electrolysis that can benefit from suitable heat integration.

blocks.label: Advanced catalysts and membranes
blocks.text: Materials designed to improve activity, durability and reduce critical-material requirements.

blocks.label: Dynamic electrolyser operation
blocks.text: Systems designed to operate alongside variable renewable electricity.

blocks.label: Digital twins and predictive maintenance
blocks.text: Models and sensor data used to estimate performance and identify degradation.

blocks.label: Hydrogen plant integration
blocks.text: Better integration of water treatment, power electronics, cooling, gas separation and downstream hydrogen use.
A strong graduate candidate should be able to:

items.text: Explain the working principles and differences between major electrolyser technologies.
Calculate theoretical hydrogen production using Faraday's law.
Estimate electrical energy consumption and system efficiency with clearly stated assumptions.
Understand stack components, materials and basic mechanical design.
Create CAD models, process diagrams and preliminary system layouts.
Develop a Python or MATLAB model of electrolyser performance.
Analyze polarization curves and interpret test data.
Identify key hydrogen hazards and understand the purpose of safety controls.
Present design decisions, calculations and limitations in a professional engineering report.

blocks.text: By graduation, aim to have two or three documented engineering projects, a practical understanding of electrochemistry and hydrogen systems, experience with CAD and modelling, and at least one internship or supervised research project if possible.
